note: From 11:13 to ~1:00:35 the lesson is a listening drill (Amal says an Arabic sentence, Medi translates); rows there are mode listening. Her Arabic in the first 3 minutes is redacted as [foreign language]. Two disputes (D3 and D4) are one moment with two different wrong pieces: D3 is kept for the clipped/MSA form of 19, D4 for the month 6-for-9; the r2 half of D3 is the same slip as D4 and is settled there. D2 and D3 are two separate attempts at the same word (19) with two separate fixes from her, so both stand. Nothing added.

row.medi_said: Does balad mean like bilad? Like, balad.
row.amal_said: [foreign language] is one, [foreign language] is multiple. ... I traveled the world.
row.right: balad = one country, bilad = countries (her explanation; her Arabic is redacted)
row.why: Didn't-know, not an error: he asked what balad is next to bilad (from the song) and she explained singular vs plural; sheet has only 'country | Dawle', so it is a new word for him.
row.english: does balad mean the same as bilad (country / countries)?

rulings.why: Real didn't-know: he asked about a word and she supplied the meaning (tier 0, signal asked). Her Arabic is redacted as [foreign language] so the row cannot quote it; confidence medium.

row.medi_said: This is it today. تسعة عشرين.
row.why: For the 19th he said tis3a 3ishrin (nine-twenty), a non-word for 19; she prompted with '19.', he moved to MSA tes3a 3ashar at 06:42, and her chat spelled the Levantine tese3ta3sh; sheet 'nineteen | tese3ta3sh | تسعتاش'.

rulings.why: Both readers saw the slip; it is a wrong number word, not a rule from buckets.md (E4 covers days/months/'on Monday', not how 19 is built), so vocab-A. 'tis3a 3ishrin' is a made-up word for 19 -> tier 1.

row.why: Second attempt at 19: after MSA tes3a 3ashar (06:42, 07:15) he clipped it to tes3ash; she recast the Levantine tese3ta3sh and typed it; a wrong form of a number he knows, sheet 'nineteen | tese3ta3sh | تسعتاش'.

rulings.why: r1 and r2 wrote different pieces for this moment. r1's piece (clipped/MSA 19 recast to tese3ta3sh) is a separate slip from D2 (different wrong form, separate fix at 07:12) and is kept here. r2's piece (month sitte for tes3a) is the same slip r1 filed as D4 and is settled under D4.

row.medi_said: I said, uh, ستة عشر ستة ... تسعش ستة.
row.why: He gave the month as sitte (6) at 06:59 and 07:10 for September (9); she queried 'ستة؟' at 07:04, recast tese3ta3sh tes3a at 07:12 and typed it; he still said تسعة عشر ستة at 07:15. Wrong number word.

rulings.why: Real and clear in the transcript: wrong number word for the month, she queried it and recast it, he repeated the error. r2 filed the same slip inside D3; one row here covers both.

row.medi_said: أب-أب المـ-امبارح. أب المامبارح or أب الامبارح? أب الامبارح.
row.amal_said: قبل امبارح or أول امبارح some people say.
row.why: For 'the day before yesterday' he deliberated and chose el- on mbaare7 (2ab(l) el-mbaare7); she recast 2abel mbaare7 / awwal mbaare7 with no el-, and he repeated أب الامبارح at 09:04; the clipped 'أب' for 2abel is S4 pronunciation and not counted.

rulings.why: Both readers saw the same slip; the piece he explicitly weighed and got wrong was the el- on mbaare7, and her recast removed it. A prefix rule from buckets.md is grammar (A1), not vocab tier 2. 'أب' for 2abel is a dropped-letter slip (S4).

row.medi_said: Uh, what you did is angry.
row.amal_said: مم. ممتاز. Let me write this one.
row.right: what you did angers / is angering (بيعصب, make-angry) - my reading
row.why: Listening: he rendered the causative bey3asseb (makes angry) as the state 'is angry'; she accepted with ممتاز. Low because one minute earlier (20:39) she accepted the parallel 'what happened is sad' for بيزعل, so she may treat this English gloss as fine.
row.english: what you did is angering / makes people angry

rulings.why: Real listening misread of make-X vs get-X (B12) that she let pass; kept low because her own acceptance of 'is sad' for بيزعل at 20:39 suggests she does not count this gloss. Amal to confirm.

row.amal_said: Mm-hmm. Did you get annoyed from what happened؟ Or of what happened؟
row.why: Listening: after fixing 'sad' to 'annoyed' he read the past انزعجتي as present 'are you annoyed'; she said Mm-hmm and recast to 'did you get annoyed' without dwelling; the Mm-hmm makes it unclear she meant it as a fix, hence low.
row.english: did you get annoyed by what happened?

rulings.why: A distinct piece from the agreed sad->annoyed slip at 24:10: tense misread of a past verb. Her full recast in the past is a fix by the brief's definition, but her Mm-hmm was acceptance, so confidence low; merger may prefer grammar-B.

row.amal_said: Yeah. That's boring. ... زهقان. Of course it's that's it. It's بس زهق، زهق.
row.why: Asked 'what's bored?' he gave the verb beyzahhe2 (she: 'that's boring'), then could not reach the adjective; she supplied zah2aan. Verb used for the adjective = wrong form of a word he knows; sheet 'bored | Zahqaan | زهقان' and 'boring / causes boredom | beyzahheq | بيزهق'.

rulings.why: Both readers saw the same slip; the brief files 'verb used as a noun/adjective' under vocab tier 2, and the fix was a whole different word shape, not an ending rule, so vocab-A tier 2 rather than grammar B15. She told him it was the wrong word ('that's boring') before supplying the right one -> explicit-no.

row.medi_said: She was happy. ... I enjoyed to it. No, Aloo, uh, Bill. Are you saying Bill?
row.amal_said: No، انبسطت له. انبسطت له. Just the verb. I got happy له. ... For، for him.
row.right: I got happy for him (انبسطت له)
row.why: Listening: he first dropped the -lo, then read la- as 'to it'; she said no, just the verb plus له = 'for him', and he fixed to 'I got happy for him' at 50:53. The preposition after انبسط sets the meaning (له for / معه with / منه because of - all drilled this lesson), so it is the verb's partner preposition.
row.english: I (or she) got happy for him

rulings.why: Same slip in both readers, only the bucket differs. This lesson drilled انبسط + له / معه / منه / لي as meaning-changing partners of the verb, which is D2 (verb + its fixed preposition); D1 kept as bucket2. The 'she' reading was not wrong (she offered enbasa6etlo too), the preposition was.

Not an error: her sheet glosses عزومة as 'house gathering / invitation | 3azoome', so his 'they enjoyed the gatherings' shows he knew the word; the only difference is an English plural in a listening gloss, and she moved on.

row.right: ألفين وستة وعشرين (alfain u sitte u 3eshreen) - my reading
row.why: For the year 2026 he said alfain u sab3a 3eshreen (seven, and no u before the tens), twice identically (06:49, 07:03); she said ممتاز at 06:56 and let it pass. Wrong number word if real; low because she is attentive to numbers and it could be a transcript garble.

rulings.why: Real if the transcript is right: sab3a for sitte is a wrong number word (vocab tier 1), and the missing u is a secondary slip with no bucket (E1 does not cover units-u-tens). Repeated identically twice so probably not ASR; kept low for Amal to confirm.
Not an error: the sheet has 'it's windy | El-denia hawa', so mish hawa for 'not windy' matches her own form; her chat summary leaving it out is not a signal.

S4 pronunciation / mis-echo, not vocab: he had already understood اتصورت as 'took a photo' (11:34) and went on with 'It's صورت. There's no preposition' (11:48); the سكرت at 11:44 is a garbled echo of the sound (possibly ASR), and she only re-said the word.

row.wrong: he will not be bored of you
row.right: ما راح يكون زهقان منك (ma ra7 ykoon zah2aan minnak)
row.why: Didn't-know: while sorting out ما راح أزهقك / يزهقك he asked how 'he will not be bored of you' is said and she supplied the ra7 ykoon zah2aan minnak form.
row.english: he will not be bored of you

rulings.why: Real didn't-know at a distinct moment from the 22:16 'he will not bore you' fix; she supplied a form he had not attempted.

row.why: Didn't-know: he asked for the 'I bore (people)' form and she gave ana bazahhe2; sheet 'i bore / make people bored | Ana bazahhe2 | بزهِّق'.
